datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer (Mini-TES) remote sensing observations (MER Spirit)
datasets.measurement_observable: Thermal infrared spectra / emissivity used to identify and characterize opaline silica (opal-A), assess viewing angle/scattering effects, and compare to laboratory spectra; includes mirror-dust correction and soil/background subtraction in some cases
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: ~340–2000 cm−1 (~5–29 µm); more usable range shown ~360–1800 cm−1; ~10 cm−1 spectral sampling
datasets.data_type_product_type: Spectra (Mini-TES ‘stare’ observations; averaged from 200 individual spectral scans plus internal blackbody calibration measurements)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Examples and constraints explicitly used include: sol 78 (surface dust reference, P3654); sol 588 (dust, sequence ID P3131); silica-rich soil Kenosha Comets observed sol 1197 P3054 (also referenced as sol 1197 P3054 in Fig. 3 inset); silica-rich outcrop Clara Zaph4 sol 1168 P3968 with adjacent soil background sol 1168 P3969; silica-rich outcrops before additional dust buildup ‘approximately sol 1220’ (17 observations noted); later North Valley silica-rich targets: Eric Frank Russell sol 1786 P3204, Stapledon sol 1788 P3205, Robert Heinlein sol 1796 P3207; additional silica-enriched float rock Fuzzy Smith observed much later sols 1805/1813/1816 (best spectrum sol 1816; sequence IDs not provided for these).
datasets.location_coverage: Gusev crater, Home Plate vicinity including Eastern Valley (e.g., Gertrude Weise trench; targets Kenosha Comets, Lefty Ganote; Clara Zaph4/Elizabeth Mahon area; Nancy Warren area), Tyrone area (Tyrone Nodules), and North Valley adjacent to the northern scarp of Home Plate (Stapledon and nearby targets).
datasets.spatial_resolution: Nominal spatial resolution 20 mrad; Mini-TES FOV described as 20 mrad (FWHM = 17.5 mrad)
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Calibrated to emissivity; mirror dust contamination correction applied to spectra (per Smith et al. [2006] approach as implemented for this work).
datasets.pds_identifiers: Mini-TES sequence IDs explicitly cited: P3654 (sol 78 dust reference); P3131 (sol 588 dust); P3054 (Kenosha Comets; sol 1197); P3968 (Clara Zaph4; sol 1168); P3969 (Clara Zaph background soil; sol 1168); P3204 (Eric Frank Russell; sol 1786); P3205 (Stapledon; sol 1788); P3207 (Robert Heinlein; sol 1796). (Paper also shows numerous Mini-TES spectra/sequence IDs in Fig. 9, but only a subset are transcribed here.)
datasets.how_used: Primary dataset for detecting opaline silica via diagnostic emissivity features (e.g., ~475 cm−1) in soils/outcrops around Home Plate; corrected for mirror-dust effects; used soil/background radiance subtraction (Clara Zaph4 vs adjacent soil) to isolate outcrop spectra; compared spectra across targets and mission times (pre- vs post-sol ~1220 dust buildup) to assess silica distribution and properties.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Panoramic Camera (Pancam) multispectral images and spectra (MER Spirit)
datasets.measurement_observable: Multispectral reflectance/relative albedo (R*) and color imaging used to (1) map the ‘hydration signature’ (934–1009 nm downturn) associated with opaline-silica-rich materials and (2) provide morphology/color context for silica-rich nodular outcrops and light-toned soils
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: 432–1009 nm through 13 filters (two redundant for stereo); hydration signature uses spectral slopes including 934–1009 nm, 754–864 nm, 436–754 nm, 864–934 nm; examples shown include R2 filter at 754 nm and a H2O-related feature near ~1000 nm
datasets.data_type_product_type: Multispectral images, mosaics/panoramas, and derived spectral parameters (‘hydration signature’ maps)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Examples explicitly cited include: sol 1198 Pancam image of Kenosha Comets (P2539); sol 1174 Pancam observation of Clara Zaph4/Elizabeth Mahon area (P2588); sol 1234 Pancam mosaic showing Nancy Warren area and crushed rocks (P2378); sol 1294 Pancam reimaging after dust fallout (P2581); sol 1183 Pancam image of Good Question scene (P2599); sol 1798 Pancam image of Stapledon and crushed rocks (P2537); plus other Pancam panorama products referenced (e.g., McMurdo, Bonestell, Calypso) without specific product IDs given in the provided text.
datasets.location_coverage: Gusev crater, Home Plate vicinity: Eastern Valley (Gertrude Weise trench and silica-rich nodular outcrops such as Clara Zaph4 and surroundings), North Valley (Stapledon), and eastern edge of Home Plate (Good Question).
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Images/spectra obtained from the Pancam website; processed mosaics/panoramas described there (calibration limitations at low Sun angles discussed, but no explicit PDS processing level stated).
datasets.pds_identifiers: Pancam product/sequence IDs explicitly cited in captions/text: P2539 (sol 1198; Kenosha Comets image); P2588 (sol 1174; Clara Zaph4 and adjacent soil); P2378 (sol 1234; mosaic including silica-rich crushed rocks and targets); P2581 (sol 1294; reimaging after dust fallout); P2599 (sol 1183; Good Question scene); P2537 (sol 1798; Stapledon scene); Pancam website URL used for products: http://marswatch.astro.cornell.edu/pancam_instrument/
datasets.how_used: Used to (a) document color/morphology of silica-rich nodular outcrops and light-toned soils, (b) compute and map the Pancam ‘hydration signature’ to identify silica-rich materials and assess variability/contamination effects, and (c) provide context for Mini-TES pointing and IDD target selection/interpretation.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS) and Mössbauer (MIMOS II) compositional/mineralogical measurements (MER Spirit)
datasets.instrument_sensor: Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS); MIMOS II Mössbauer spectrometer
datasets.measurement_observable: Elemental chemistry (Na to Y) from APXS and Fe-mineralogy/Fe oxidation state (Fe3+/Fetotal) plus alteration-phase proportions (MAI) from Mössbauer; used to quantify SiO2 enrichment, assess contamination by soil/dust, and evaluate alteration/redox indicators relevant to silica origin
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ contact compositional analyses (APXS elemental abundances; Mössbauer spectra-derived mineralogy/parameters)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Targets/sols explicitly compiled/used include (Table 2 and text): Lefty Ganote soil (sol 1199), Kenosha Comets soil (sol 1190/1189 in Table 1 vs Table 2; Kenosha Comets APXS entry is sol 1190 in Table 2), Nancy Warren outcrop (sol 1225), Elizabeth Mahon outcrop (sol 1157), Norma Luker rock (sol 1288), Fuzzy Smith rock (sol 770), Innocent Bystander rock (sol 1251), Good Question outcrop (sol 1179), Calibration Soil (sol 1230). Mössbauer measurements applied to the same silica-rich materials except Norma Luker (explicitly excluded). Stapledon APXS measurement referenced as ~72 wt% SiO2 (Spirit winter campaign; sol not specified for APXS in provided text).
datasets.location_coverage: Gusev crater, Home Plate vicinity: Eastern Valley targets around Home Plate (including Gertrude Weise trench area and Nancy Warren/Virginia Bell vicinity), eastern edge of Home Plate (Good Question), and on top of Home Plate (Fuzzy Smith). Calibration Soil located within ~0.5 m of Nancy Warren in Eastern Valley.
datasets.spatial_resolution: APXS effective FOV ~25 mm diameter (maximum 38 mm); Mössbauer beam diameter ~14 mm (both stated)
datasets.pds_identifiers: No PDS LIDs/DATA_SET_IDs provided in the paper text. Identifiers provided are target names and sol numbers (e.g., ‘sol 1230 Calibration Soil’, ‘sol 1157 Elizabeth Mahon’, ‘sol 1225 Nancy Warren’, etc.) and the statement that APXS data presented are from Ming et al. (2008) except Stapledon; Mössbauer data presented are from Morris et al. (2008).
datasets.how_used: APXS compositions were used to quantify SiO2 (and other elements) in silica-rich soils/outcrops and to perform linear soil-subtraction corrections using ‘Calibration Soil’ as the contaminant endmember; Mössbauer-derived mineralogy and Fe redox/alteration indices were used to assess alteration style, oxidation state, and to evaluate hypotheses for silica formation (leaching vs precipitation).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Microscopic Imager (MI) images of rocks/soils (MER Spirit)
datasets.measurement_observable: Microscale morphology/texture of silica-rich nodular outcrops, crushed rock interiors, and silica-rich soils (porosity, brecciation/clasts, trapped soil grains)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Microscopic images (single frames, focus stacks, mosaics; stereo anaglyphs in some cases)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: MI observations explicitly discussed include: Puenta Arenas (sol 1101); Elizabeth Mahon mosaic (sol 1157); Kenosha Comets MI mosaic (sol 1189); Lefty Ganote MI mosaic (sol 1198); Nancy Warren MI mosaic (sol 1225); Darlene Mickelsen MI mosaic (sol 1232); Innocent Bystander MI mosaics/frames (sols 1251 and 1252); Norma Luker MI (sol 1291); Stapledon MI mosaic (sol 1796).
datasets.location_coverage: Gusev crater, Home Plate vicinity (Eastern Valley and North Valley) including targets near Gertrude Weise trench (silica-rich soils), silica-rich nodular outcrops (e.g., Elizabeth Mahon, Nancy Warren), and crushed silica-rich rocks (Innocent Bystander, Norma Luker), plus North Valley outcrop Stapledon.
datasets.spatial_resolution: 30 µm/pixel across a 31 × 31 mm field of view (FOV)
datasets.pds_identifiers: Paper states MI single-frame images (and some stereo anaglyphs) are available from the PDS Analyst’s Notebook: http://an.rsl.wustl.edu/mer/ (mosaics noted as not available there). No specific MI product IDs are provided in the text.
datasets.how_used: Used to document and interpret microtextures (porosity, sponge-like textures, clastic/brecciated fabrics, soil contamination) of silica-rich targets and to support hypotheses about formation processes (e.g., sinter-like precipitation vs leaching residue) and contamination effects on compositional/spectral datasets.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: HiRISE image PSP_001513_1655_RED of Home Plate and vicinity
datasets.measurement_observable: Orbital imaging used for geologic context and mapping of Home Plate region and silica-rich outcrop occurrences/labels
datasets.location_coverage: Gusev crater, Home Plate and vicinity (includes labeled silica-rich nodular outcrops and soil targets; Spirit location at Low Ridge during second Martian winter mentioned in caption)
datasets.how_used: Provided regional context map (Figure 1) to show distribution of silica-rich nodular outcrops/soils around Home Plate and to relate rover-observed targets to orbital-scale geomorphology.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: For Spirit rover operations in Gusev crater near Home Plate (including disturbed soils and nodular outcrops), use Mini-TES unitless thermal-infrared emissivity spectra (5–29 µm; ~10 cm⁻¹ sampling) to map occurrences of opaline silica via the diagnostic low-wavenumber emissivity minimum and evaluate whether spectral signatures are consistent with porous sinter versus leached residues, accounting for viewing-geometry and scattering effects.

Reprocess Spirit rover Mini-TES raw “stare” observations (multiple-scan acquisitions with internal blackbody measurements) spanning pre- and post-mirror dust contamination intervals to quantify calibration drift and test alternative mirror-dust correction strategies, with emphasis on preserving weak spectral features relevant to silica detection in the Home Plate campaign.

output_parsed.paper_title: Characteristics, distribution, origin, and significance of opaline silica observed by the Spirit rover in Gusev crater, Mars

queries.query: For the Spirit rover traverse in Gusev crater during the Home Plate campaign (roughly sols 1100–1300), compile APXS-derived major-element oxide abundances for silica-enriched light-toned soils and nodular outcrops and apply a two-component soil/dust contamination correction using a nearby undisturbed regolith endmember to estimate intrinsic SiO2 enrichment and associated element trends (e.g., TiO2) relevant to hydrothermal alteration models.

Using Spirit rover Mössbauer measurements from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater, quantify Fe-bearing phase proportions to estimate oxidation state and alteration indices (primary silicates/oxides versus alteration-related ferric phases) and compare silica-rich nodular outcrops/soils against adjacent volcanic and sulfate-bearing materials to test leaching versus precipitation scenarios.

queries.query: Assemble the raw Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager observations of the Martian surface (single frames plus multi-image focus sequences and close-up mosaics) needed to characterize microscale textures of altered materials in Gusev crater (e.g., porous nodular outcrops and disturbed wheel-trench soils) at ~30 µm/pixel under broadband visible illumination.

Retrieve the calibrated Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager science image collection for quantitative texture analysis of silica-enriched materials in Gusev crater (void fraction/microporosity, clast-supported vs matrix-supported fabrics, and trapped soil-grain contamination) using broadband visible (400–700 nm) close-up imaging products.

final_output.query: For Spirit rover operations in Gusev crater near Home Plate (including disturbed soils and nodular outcrops), use Mini-TES unitless thermal-infrared emissivity spectra (5–29 µm; ~10 cm⁻¹ sampling) to map occurrences of opaline silica via the diagnostic low-wavenumber emissivity minimum and evaluate whether spectral signatures are consistent with porous sinter versus leached residues, accounting for viewing-geometry and scattering effects.

Reprocess Spirit rover Mini-TES raw “stare” observations (multiple-scan acquisitions with internal blackbody measurements) spanning pre- and post-mirror dust contamination intervals to quantify calibration drift and test alternative mirror-dust correction strategies, with emphasis on preserving weak spectral features relevant to silica detection in the Home Plate campaign.

MER Spirit Pancam: identify the radiometrically calibrated right-eye R2 (754 nm) scene acquired on sol 1174 in Gusev crater near the Home Plate region (Eastern Valley), constrained to the acquisition time 2007-04-23T07:04:55Z, for deriving 13-filter multispectral slope products (including the 934–1009 nm downturn) used to map the hydration signature of opaline-silica-rich materials.

MER Spirit Pancam: identify the radiometrically calibrated right-eye R2 (754 nm) scene acquired on sol 1798 in Gusev crater near the northern Home Plate scarp (North Valley), constrained to the acquisition time 2009-01-23T10:44:21Z, to quantify multispectral reflectance/color context for silica-rich nodular outcrops and adjacent light-toned/disturbed surface materials.

For the Spirit rover traverse in Gusev crater during the Home Plate campaign (roughly sols 1100–1300), compile APXS-derived major-element oxide abundances for silica-enriched light-toned soils and nodular outcrops and apply a two-component soil/dust contamination correction using a nearby undisturbed regolith endmember to estimate intrinsic SiO2 enrichment and associated element trends (e.g., TiO2) relevant to hydrothermal alteration models.

Using Spirit rover Mössbauer measurements from the Home Plate vicinity in Gusev crater, quantify Fe-bearing phase proportions to estimate oxidation state and alteration indices (primary silicates/oxides versus alteration-related ferric phases) and compare silica-rich nodular outcrops/soils against adjacent volcanic and sulfate-bearing materials to test leaching versus precipitation scenarios.

Assemble the raw Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager observations of the Martian surface (single frames plus multi-image focus sequences and close-up mosaics) needed to characterize microscale textures of altered materials in Gusev crater (e.g., porous nodular outcrops and disturbed wheel-trench soils) at ~30 µm/pixel under broadband visible illumination.

Retrieve the calibrated Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager science image collection for quantitative texture analysis of silica-enriched materials in Gusev crater (void fraction/microporosity, clast-supported vs matrix-supported fabrics, and trapped soil-grain contamination) using broadband visible (400–700 nm) close-up imaging products.

I need the single Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE red-channel map-projected reduced-data-record scene covering the Home Plate feature in Gusev crater, where the Spirit rover is parked at Low Ridge (second winter), to use as an orbital basemap for mapping silica-rich nodular outcrop distribution.

Assemble the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE map-projected reduced-data-record imaging dataset for Mars so I can pull consistent high-resolution context frames for geomorphic mapping of hydrothermal silica-bearing terrains, including the Home Plate region in Gusev crater.
